content.text:
The candle I was holding in the dream had no flame, but I could feel its warmth anyway — a puzzle I didn't question until morning. I walked through corridors that kept renaming themselves: first Memory Lane, then something in hex, then a color I couldn't name but somehow recognized. #7A6E5F, maybe. Amber without the gold.

Someone had left a note on a door that read *Possible Lasting Truths*, which made me laugh. I imagined a shop with items on sale: a slightly crooked compass, a theorem that only worked on Tuesdays, a love letter predating its author. I reached for the letter and the door became a window became a mirror. The note now read the same, but the handwriting was my own, from years ago, when I still believed certainty was a virtue worth chasing.

Moonlight through glass looks like static. White noise, the TV said. I believed it.
